data.name: Wilfrid
data.gender_notes: Wilfrid is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic elements ‘wulf’ (wolf) and ‘frith’ (peace). The name Wilfrid means ‘friend of peace.’ In the Middle Ages, the name was popular among monks and hermits, who sought to live in peace and harmony with nature. The name Wilfrid carries the meaning “Friend of peace” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Wilfrid usually hope their child will grow to embody friend of peace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes peace, harmony, and spiritual strength.
data.etymology: Wilfrid belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friend of peace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Wilfrid total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: וִילְפְרִיד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ווילפריד הוא שם גבור, גבורה ועז, וכוח. זהו שם שנקבע על ידי האנגלו-סקסונים, ומקור השם הוא בהברה הגרמאנית. השם נזכר בהיסטוריה כבעל אומץ, ובעל כוח. זהו שם שניתן במסורת הנוצרית, וזכור ביום הזיכרון לעדים הקדושים.

in_greek.name: Γιίλφρηδ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Ὀνοματεύεται Γίλφρηδ (Γιίλφρηδ) εἶναι ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ ῥησαρμός, καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς δύναμης. Ἡ ρίζα τοῦ ὀνόματος εἶναι ἡ ἡלικίας, τὸ ἡλικόν. Ἡ ἡλικία εἶναι ἡ ἡλικία τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ τοῦ σώματος. Ὅταν πνεῦμα καὶ σῶμα εἰσιν ἕνωται, τότε ἐπιτυγχάνει ἡ ἰσχύς καὶ ῥησαρμός. Ἔτσι, ὁ Γίλφρηδ εἶναι ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ ῥησαρμός, καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς δύναμης.

in_latin.name: Wilfridus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Wilfridus significat fortitudo, virtus, robur. Origine, nomen Wilfridus derivatur ex lingua Germanica. In historia, Wilfridus notus est vir fortis, vir robur, virtus. Nomen Wilfridus in traditione Christiana usitatum est, et memoriae dignus est in die commemorationis Martyrum Sanctorum.

in_english.name: Wilfrid
in_english.long_meaning: Wilfrid is a name that signifies courage, strength, power, valor, and bravery. It originated from the Germanic language and was used by the Anglo-Saxons. In history, Wilfrid is remembered as a man of great courage, strength, and power. In Christian tradition, Wilfrid is a name that is associated with the qualities of a saint, and is remembered on the day of remembrance for the Witnesses of the Faith.

data.cultural_impact: The name Wilfrid is deeply rooted in Germanic and Anglo-Saxon history. It was a name borne by several notable figures, including Saint Wilfrid of York, an English bishop and missionary who played a critical role in spreading Christianity in Europe during the early Middle Ages. The name Wilfrid is often associated with strength and leadership, as the wolf symbolized power and protection in Germanic mythology. As a result, bearers of this name were seen as brave, strong, and noble leaders who could inspire others to seek peace and harmony.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Wilfrid represents the inherent human desire for peace and harmony amidst the chaos and turmoil of the world. The name serves as a reminder that despite the challenges and conflicts that arise in life, we can always strive to maintain inner peace and seek reconciliation with others. It also reflects the Christian virtue of peacemaking, encouraging individuals to be messengers of God's love and offer forgiveness and reconciliation to those in need. Ultimately, the name Wilfrid embodies the hope that through inner peace and spiritual growth, one can become a ‘friend of God’ and a source of comfort and inspiration to others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Wilfrid: Derived from Old English elements 'wulf' meaning wolf and 'frith' meaning peace, Wilfrid signifies a warrior or protector who brings peace. In a spiritual sense, it represents the inner strength and courage needed to maintain harmony in the midst of challenges.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Saint Wilfrid was a 7th-century bishop of York. The name Wilfrid carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Wilfrid remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: David Wilfrid, a minister in Dublin, Ireland, shares that their name Wilfrid meaning "Friend of peace" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
